questions.stem: The first action when someone falls overboard is:
options: Call Mayday on Channel 16 before doing anything else
Shout, point and throw a flotation device
Stop the engine and drop the anchor
Turn sharply and go full speed back

questions.stem: A person assigned to point at someone in the water should:
options: Help steer the boat back to them
Fetch the first aid kit and blankets from below
Keep watching and pointing, nothing else
Get the boat hook and ladder ready

questions.stem: When approaching a person in the water, you should arrange to have them:
options: On the leeward side
On the windward side
Behind the propeller
In the wake
questions.explanation: The boat then drifts toward them.

questions.stem: When close to a person in the water, the engine should be:
options: In full ahead
In neutral or off
In full astern
In slow ahead
Starts the engine
Anchors the boat
Calls the Coast Guard
Marks the position

questions.stem: The danger of cold water in the first minutes is:
options: Cold shock
Seasickness
Dehydration
Sunburn

questions.stem: You should enter the water to rescue someone:
options: Straight away, before telling anyone else on board
Only as a last resort and in a lifejacket
Without gear, so you can swim faster
As the first choice, to save time

questions.stem: The master's report of a serious marine occurrence normally includes:
options: Only a bill for the damage
No report if no one is hurt
Only a text message to the owner about the damage
An initial report then a follow-up
questions.explanation: Check the rules for your vessel.

questions.stem: To help prevent falls overboard you should:
options: Wear a lifejacket and keep decks clear and non-slip
Stand on the bow to watch the waves
Move quickly on deck to finish jobs
Walk along the gunwale to save time
